newsitem.title: USA: IMF board to consider funding for debt initiative.
newsitem.headline: IMF board to consider funding for debt initiative.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund executive board will consider the initial financing for the debt initiative for heavily indebted poor countries in the next few weeks, a senior IMF official said Thursday.

Jack Boorman, Director of the IMF's policy development and review department, said he also believed that some five or six countries would receive a commitment for assistance before the spring meetings of the IMF and World Bank take place in April.

Speaking at an IMF-sponsored economic forum to discuss the initiative, Boorman said the initial funding would allow the program to get underway while the IMF permanent funding, which could include the sale of some IMF gold, is completed.
"The board has agreed in principle that we can on a temporary basis use some of the resources that are in a reserve account," Boorman told reporters after the meeting.
"We have put specific decisions to the board that will permit the use of some of those monies in this initial period," he added.

He said he was asking permission from the board to transfer a portion of those funds from the reserve account for use in the initiative. He decline to say how much will be requested but that it would be "a fraction" of the close to 2 billion Special Drawing Rights in the reserve account.

The World Bank, for its part of the debt initiative for the very poorest countries, has put some $500 million into a trust account for the iniative and President James Wolfensohn has said that further allocations would be made when needed.

During the economic forum, Masood Ahmed, director of the World Bank's international economics department, said it was important that the funding be substantial enough to keep the program from failing.
It is designed through loan forgiveness, grants and other measures, to allow countries to reduce the amount of debt to sustainable levels.
